verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is publicly readable: the getsentry/sentry GitHub repo is cited, the docs say you can run all of Sentry on your own server for free, and a community user credits the visible source with helping advanced integrations. However, community reports say Sentry relicensed to the BSL, a source-available rather than OSI-open license, and one user now treats it as closed-source, so the 'open license' half of the story is only partly met. Missing for 10: an OSI-approved open-source license for the core product, first-party license documentation in the evidence, and explicit confirmation of which components (SDKs vs. server) carry which license.
